scope: Material texture admission based on decoded pixels, with a larger file allowance and unchanged project asset budget
changes: All material-set, individual-slot, ORM and worker paths share a 256 MiB file allowance. A 4K RGBA16 source plus metadata fits.
PNG/JPEG/WebP headers are checked before browser thumbnails and decoding. TIFF/TGA workers retain dimension checks before pixel allocation.
All material inputs use a 16-megapixel decoded-image bound; project Apply retains the existing 384 MiB distinct-asset budget.
PNG conversion supports source dimensions beyond the previous 2048-pixel render-size assumption, up to 16 MP / 8192 per side.
Serialized texture data URLs and native package image chunks accept the larger maps. Model/environment limits remain unchanged.
Material channel buffers transfer to the inline worker without structured-clone copies.
Portable surface presets retain their separate 128 MiB synchronous JSON limit; large native projects remain the appropriate container when a preset exceeds it.

checks.build: npm run build: passed, including typecheck, runtime/declarations and editor build. Existing bundle-size warnings remain.

coverage: Real 4096x4096 uncompressed BGRA TGA with seeded, difficult-to-compress pixels: 67,108,882 bytes. ORM channel output matches the source.
Full material preview/apply embeds PNG exceeding the former 28-million-character schema ceiling. PNG dimensions and first pixel independently checked with sharp.
Native download, undo, redo, IndexedDB autosave/reload and exact SHA-256 match of the restored embedded texture.

33 MiB schema fixture round-trips through native packages, exceeding both the former schema and 32 MB package limits. Shared project asset-budget enforcement and unchanged model rejection also checked.
File/decoded-dimension boundary checks; independent PNG, baseline/progressive JPEG, lossy/lossless/extended WebP fixtures; truncated headers and cancellation.
Small PNG/JPEG/WebP headers declaring 8192x8192 images are rejected before browser allocation. Chrome confirms no thumbnail, unchanged committed document, and successful replacement/retry.
Existing engine conversions, alpha/precision, cancellation, failure retry, history, rendering and worker-startup recovery scenarios.
limitations: Windows/installed Chrome with --enable-unsafe-swiftshader only; no cross-device or cross-browser certification.
The 4K case is a deterministic synthetic texture, not a broad vendor-asset survey or peak-memory benchmark.
File and pixel limits bound individual inputs; they are not a guarantee of maximum process memory for every multi-map batch.
PNG numeric decoding and TIFF/TGA conversion retain an 8192-per-side bound in addition to pixel count; render texture arrays remain 256-2048 per side.
Surface presets keep the separate 128 MiB JSON limit. Terrain geometry/brush-alpha imports keep their existing limits.
